target.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw does not currently have an official installable MXC sandbox backend for Windows hosts that can run sandboxed commands through Microsoft eXecution Containers. This leaves MXC-capable Windows environments without a first-party plugin path for ProcessContainer-backed execution and filesystem bridge operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an official OpenShell-style external `mxc` sandbox plugin package (`@openclaw/mxc-sandbox`) with Windows-only readiness checks, plugin-owned MXC SDK dependency ownership, ProcessContainer payload construction, a plugin-side launcher, host-backed filesystem bridge support, sandbox policy loading, and targeted tests.

The plugin source lives under `extensions/mxc`, but it is packaged as an installable plugin (`bundledDist: false`) so the MXC SDK/native dependency is owned by the plugin package instead of an unshipped bundled `node_modules` tree. The backend uses the current MXC `0.7.0-alpha` schema and keeps sandbox defaults conservative: strict plugin config, read-only isolated workspaces for `none`, a distinct read-only agent workspace for `ro`, writable agent workspaces for `rw`, fail-closed protected-skill overlap handling, guarded fs-safe host mutations, required explicit policy files/paths, and host-derived Windows baseline roots.

The MXC read-only skill mount resolver remains plugin-local instead of adding a plugin-specific public sandbox SDK export. The only new shared SDK surface is the narrow generic fs-safe recursive-remove seam requested by review because the sandbox bridge contract includes `recursive`/`force` behavior that the pinned fs-safe `Root.remove` API does not expose.

## User Impact

Users on MXC-capable Windows hosts can install the official MXC sandbox plugin, restart the Gateway, configure `sandbox.backend: "mxc"`, and run OpenClaw sandboxed commands through MXC. Non-Windows or unsupported Windows hosts remain unaffected because the plugin stays dormant when readiness probes fail.

Install command:

```bash
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mxc-sandbox
```

## Evidence

Related: https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/issues/626

AI-assisted: yes. The implementation and review-response pass used Copilot CLI, with every accepted review finding checked against current OpenClaw code, the pinned fs-safe API, the MXC SDK source/types, focused tests, and native Windows behavior.

### Final review-response refresh (2026-07-10)

- Final pushed head: `92f6e6d62780c52a11976cc06ae0f3b76488a096`.
- Rebase base used for the validated pass: `2f9cb9200669fe5df86fd229b445685e9b1b81b1` (`upstream/main` at rebase time).
- The first eight commits replayed with exact equality (`=`). The final SDK-surface commit changed only its pinned export budget to match current main: 10,494 public exports / 5,237 callable exports.
- Addressed the July 10 review:
  - `workspaceAccess: "ro"` now maps the distinct agent workspace read-only in both ProcessContainer policy and the fs bridge.
  - host mkdir/remove/rename operations now use fs-safe Root operations; recursive removal uses one narrow shared fs-safe seam with force/not-found and rebind-race coverage.
  - configured policy files and explicit filesystem paths now fail closed with source/path provenance.
  - MXC config now follows the strict OpenShell-style Zod/plugin-schema pattern with the Node-safe timer cap and manifest parity.
  - container policy construction is split from execution lifecycle and uses the MXC SDK `ContainerConfig` type.
  - generic `bundledDist: false` static-asset behavior has direct regression coverage.
  - the MXC README and Chinese glossary are current.

### Linux validation

Local WSL2 `Ubuntu-24.04`, isolated Linux-filesystem clones, Node `v24.13.0`, pnpm `11.2.2`:

- final-head Oxfmt check and `git diff --check` passed.
- focused MXC/fs-safe/plugin-SDK/runtime-postbuild tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension mxc` passed: 8 files passed / 2 Windows-only files skipped; 57 tests passed / 52 skipped.
- `pnpm check:test-types` passed.
- `pnpm build` passed on production-equivalent head `104bc7aad8d3d63ebc2659dd0ea20dee96b23318`; the final delta only updates `extensions/mxc/test/mxc-backend.test.ts`.
- plugin inventory, docs map, i18n glossary, and changed-shrinkwrap checks passed before the final test-only delta.
- `pnpm check:changed` could not run locally because its selected Crabbox/Testbox binary failed its own `--version`/`--help` sanity check on both candidate and base; this is environment/tooling, not candidate-specific.

### Native Windows validation

SSH target `adminuser@172.19.169.53`, exact final head, Node `v24.18.0`, pnpm `11.2.2`:

- focused MXC tests passed: 2 files / 52 tests.
- `pnpm test:extension mxc` passed: 10 files / 109 tests.
- plugin-specific runtime build passed with `node scripts/lib/plugin-npm-runtime-build.mjs extensions/mxc`.
- packed `openclaw-mxc-sandbox-2026.6.11.tgz`: 32 files, including `package/dist/index.js`, `package/dist/mxc-spawn-launcher.mjs`, and `package/npm-shrinkwrap.json`.
- managed `npm-pack:` install passed; `openclaw plugins inspect mxc --runtime --json` reported `status: "loaded"` from isolated managed plugin state.
- native `wxc-exec.exe` ProcessContainer smoke passed:
  - `MXC_PROCESSCONTAINER_OK`.
  - `none` denied access to the distinct agent workspace.
  - `ro` allowed reads and denied mutation.
  - `rw` persisted `MXC_RW_MARKER`.
  - protected skill overlap failed closed.
  - missing configured policy file/path failed closed.

### Review closeout

Copilot autoreview was split into complete production, test, and docs bundles because the single complete PR bundle exceeded Copilot's input limit.

- production/docs bundles were clean after review-response updates.
- Copilot identified a binary-override test mock that did not exercise the configured path; the mock/assertion now verify the real wiring.
- Copilot questioned `rw` protected-skill behavior; direct MXC source inspection and native Windows proof confirm a nested read-only grant does not override a writable parent, so the overlap guard remains intentionally fail-closed and the README now states that limitation accurately.
- follow-up commit reviews for `104bc7aad8` and `c0a242c368` exited clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- CI lint follow-up `ab74106328` fixes the two extension Oxlint findings (`import type` and preserved caught-error cause); targeted Oxlint and Copilot autoreview are clean.
- SDK surface follow-up `92f6e6d627` moves recursive removal out of broad `infra-runtime` and keeps it only on focused `file-access-runtime`. After rebasing onto current main, the compact-shard test, surface check, focused tests, MXC extension suite, test types, SDK package boundary check, full WSL2 build, and Copilot autoreview are clean.

### Remaining maintainer gates

- `dependency-guard` is expected to require maintainer/admin/secops approval for the intentional `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`, packaged native executors, and `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.13` dependency graph.
- The MXC SDK currently base64-encodes the full config envelope onto `wxc-exec` argv. Base64 is not secrecy; maintainers should explicitly accept this preview-SDK boundary or wait for the non-argv transport tracked in microsoft/mxc#626.
- Upstream `main` advanced after the validated rebase; the PR may show as behind even though the pushed candidate and evidence above are internally consistent.
